Objects.name: ULSDVOBJ_EIGC_BLE_Config_v1
Objects.description: Configuration of the BMD-345 BLE module on the ULS-XX-EIGC-G3. Owned by the module itself, not by the STM32: the module is a separate node on the ULS bus, reached through the STM32 USART4 link. See devs-nrf/RADIO.md for the link design these fields configure

variables.name: name
variables.description: Name. Shown by ULS Tools in the scan list and carried in the service advertisement, never in the telemetry beacon

variables.name: ctrl
variables.description: Module function enable bits. Default 15 = telemetry_enable | service_adv_enable | require_bonding | coded_phy_enable. require_bonding is on by default deliberately: the service link can write config and push firmware, so an unbonded peer must not have it

variables.name: devID
variables.description: Module ID number. Matches the devID of the STM32 it is fitted to

variables.name: fleetId
variables.description: Fleet this unit belongs to. Beacons carrying a different fleetId are dropped before the signature is even checked, so several operators can share a zone. Not a secret and not a security boundary on its own - the fleet key is what makes a beacon trustworthy

variables.name: txPower
variables.description: Requested transmit power. The achievable maximum depends on whether the SKY66112 front end is enabled and on the antenna fitted to the U.FL

variables.name: telemetryRateFar
variables.description: Beacon rate used beyond nearRange, on Coded PHY. This is the advertising interval - in a connectionless design the beacon rate and the advertising rate are one number, not two. Keep it low: every device in the zone shares the three primary advertising channels

variables.name: telemetryRateNear
variables.description: Beacon rate used within nearRange, where the 1M PHY is enough and airtime per beacon is far cheaper

variables.name: nearRange
variables.description: Distance to the peer below which the module switches from Coded PHY at telemetryRateFar to 1M PHY at telemetryRateNear. Zero pins it to the far setting

variables.name: beaconMaxAge
variables.description: A received beacon older than this by the receiver's own GNSS clock is discarded as a replay. Wants to be larger than the worst GNSS time offset between two units and smaller than any useful replay window

variables.name: serviceAdvTimeout
variables.description: Connectable service advertising stops this long after boot, leaving a deployed unit with no connectable surface at all - it only broadcasts. Zero means advertise forever, which is for the bench

variables.name: peerSerials
variables.description: Serial numbers of the peers this unit will talk to. All zero means accept any peer of the same fleet whose beacon signature verifies. This narrows an already authenticated set - it is not what keeps strangers out
